# 黃籙九陽梵炁燈儀

**ID:** KR5a0212
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0212

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

An eleven-folio *Huánglù* 黃籙 (Yellow Register) lamp-liturgy for the "Brahman Energies of the Nine Yáng" (*Jiǔyáng fànqì* 九陽梵氣), understood here as the *qì* of the Nine Heavens, which illuminate the underworld and enable the souls of the deceased to ascend. The rite invokes a suite of presiding deities — Tàiyǐ jiùkǔ tiānzūn 太乙救苦天尊, the Jiǔtiān shēngshén shàngdì 九天生神上帝, the Jiǔyáng fànqì tiānjūn 九陽梵炁天君, the *jiǔzhōu shèlìng* 九州社令 territorial deities, and the full complement of underworld officials of the Nine Depths (*Jiǔyōu dìyù* 九幽地獄) — then, at each of the nine cardinal stations, summons the *Jiùkǔ tiānzūn* 救苦天尊 of that direction, lights a lamp, and chants the corresponding hymn drawn from *[DZ 318 Dòngxuán língbǎo zìrán jiǔtiān shēngshén zhāngjīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0318)*.

**Abstract**

John Lagerwey, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:968–969 (§3.B.1, Zhèngyī), glosses the "Nine Yáng Brahman Energies" as the *qì* of the Nine Heavens, held to light the underworld and enable the ascent of the souls of the dead. The liturgical skeleton consists of directional invocations to the *Jiǔkǔ tiānzūn* with lamp-lightings, each followed by the appropriate hymn drawn from [DZ 318](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0318). The frontmatter brackets composition broadly 1100–1300, within the normal Sòng-era *Huánglù* ritual cycle.
